newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia must cut gov't spending further - cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Colombia must cut gov't spending further - cenbank.

text.p: Colombia faces the risk of a sharp acceleration in inflation, a much weaker peso and an extended period of slow economic growth unless the government cuts public spending further, the central bank said Thursday.

In its half-year report to Congress, the board of directors of the central bank said recent fiscal adjustments and the government's 1998 budget -- one of the most austere in years -- were not enough to prevent severe economic problems.
"The truth is that the current trend in public finances is not sustainable in the medium term," the report said.
"Without a timely solution, we will be moving down the path of a precarious macroeconomic situation which is highly vulnerable to external factors," it added.

After the report, President Ernesto Samper said he agreed there were several medium and long-term "time bombs" threatening the public-sector finances, including pensions payments and hefty financial transfers from central government to local and regional administrative bodies.
"The medium- and long-term situation is worrying...unless we carry out thorough surgery on the budget and fiscal system," Samper told reporters.
"The bank is right to sound the alarm bells and...we should sit down and find medium and long-term solutions," he added.
In its statement to Congress, the bank forecasts the central government's budget deficit will grow to 4.2 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1998 from about 4.1 percent this year.

To be sure, the bank acknowledged the government's drive to slash spending, as its 1998 budget of 25.9 trillion pesos, excluding debt servicing, came in four percent lower in real terms than the current year's budget.
